clue.text: Uplifting tune after a song

indicators.note: in a down light, lifting up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A melody that lifts the spirits plays after a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uplifting' turns the whole run AIR + A upwards in this down entry, giving ARIA.
explanation.definitionFit: An operatic solo piece for one voice is a kind of song.

clue.text: L — obsolete party and I'm flipping leading it!

indicators.note: the earlier pieces are placed in front of the and that follows
flipping turns the two letters of the contraction over so they read backwards

parts.note: the Liberal Party, the Lib of old, merged away in 1988
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a defunct party is led by them, of all people.
explanation.walkthrough: Throughout this puzzle L stands for a Labour leader and C for a Conservative one. 'flipping' reverses I'M to MI.
explanation.definitionFit: Ed Miliband led the Labour Party from 2010, which is what the theme's L stands for.

clue.text: L to pay

definitions.meaning: a Labour leader, by the puzzle's theme
to ... the bill is to pay it

explanation.definitionFit: Michael Foot was leader of the Labour Party, and footing a bill means settling it.

clue.text: C — parliament's ultimate mother hen?

indicators.note: ultimate picks the final letter of the word parliament

parts.note: a sitting hen is one that hatches eggs, a hatcher

explanation.surface: A Conservative leader cast as the fussing mother hen of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Thatcher led the Conservative Party, the theme's C, from 1975 to 1990.

clue.text: Totally exposed, run end of spear into cut

indicators.note: into says the picked letter goes inside the cut of meat

parts.note: a steak is a cut of meat

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of spear

explanation.surface: Stripped bare, a hunter drives the spear's point into a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: To streak is to run naked through a public place, a run with nothing on.

clue.text: Ancient celebration, beautiful game ends anagrammatically for this year's crossword anniversary?

indicators.note: the word itself announces that the letters are to be rearranged
ends takes the final letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: An old festivity for the beautiful game is offered as a crossword birthday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' gives N, L, E, which join ANCIENT to be rearranged. The puzzle ran in 2013, a hundred years after the first crossword appeared in 1913.
explanation.definitionFit: A hundredth anniversary is a centenary, and the crossword was born in 1913.

clue.text: Among extremists in archipelago I wander northwards slowly

indicators.note: among puts the turned letters between the two picked end letters
the extremists in a word are its first and last letters
in a down light, going north reads the letters from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to gad about is to wander

explanation.surface: Someone drifts north between the outlying islands at an easy pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northwards' turns I GAD into DAGI, which sits between A and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is the musical direction for a slow tempo, slowly.

clue.text: C's Project?

definitions.meaning: a Conservative leader, by the puzzle's theme
the ... Project is a set of giant domed greenhouses in Cornwall, England

explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Eden was Conservative Prime Minister, and the Eden Project is a Cornish attraction.

clue.text: One so thick-skinned audibly mocking foreign drama

indicators.note: audibly says the letters come from how the phrase sounds when said

parts.note: wry means mocking, and Noh is classical Japanese theatre

explanation.surface: A heckler so thick-skinned they sneer out loud at overseas theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal has notoriously tough hide, so it is the type of a thick-skinned creature.

clue.text: Rash above the neck inflamed, then?

definitions.meaning: a literal reading: hot in the head, the bit above the neck

explanation.definitionFit: Someone impetuous and quick to anger is rash, acting without thought.

clue.text: Child in Israel misconstrued polymath

indicators.note: in places the young one inside the rearranged country name
misconstrued means wrongly put together, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A child in Israel is misunderstood as a great all-round thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Child in Israel' reads like a news story, but the country's name is only fodder for 'misconstrued'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek philosopher wrote on logic, biology, ethics and more, a model of wide learning.

clue.text: No unpleasant type rejected an unusual cat

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the run is read in reverse

parts.note: a git is British slang for an unpleasant person

explanation.surface: An unpleasant type turns down an exotic cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unpleasant type' is British slang usage; 'rejected' turns the whole two-word phrase round, not just one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The offspring of a male tiger and a lioness is a rare hybrid big cat.

clue.text: Submissive prodigal son comes first

indicators.note: comes first puts the single letter in front of the other piece

parts.note: prodigal means lavish, extravagantly generous

explanation.surface: The prodigal son returns, humble, and is put first.
explanation.definitionFit: Being servile, abjectly obedient, is being submissive.

clue.text: Author up tree

indicators.note: in a down light, up reads the name from the bottom

parts.note: Albert Camus, French author of The Outsider

explanation.surface: A writer has climbed a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: This shrub or small tree has red berries used as a spice.

clue.text: Render bite when barking, as cross

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters go wild and are reordered

explanation.surface: A mad dog will give a bite, so be wary of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' is British slang for mad, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross breeds or species is to mate them, to produce a hybrid.

clue.text: L batting during innings

indicators.note: during places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a knock is a cricket innings
in cricket the side that is in is batting

explanation.surface: A Labour leader is at the crease through his innings.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil Kinnock led the Labour Party from 1983 to 1992, the theme's L.

clue.text: Passage from paperback or another good book

indicators.note: Passage from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A selection taken from one paperback or another is a fine read.
explanation.definitionFit: The holy book of Islam is a scripture, a good book like the Bible.

clue.text: Centre with C central to empty speaking?

indicators.note: central to places the leader's initials in the middle of the other piece

parts.note: the letters M and T said out loud sound like the word empty
a Conservative leader: Iain Duncan Smith, initials IDS, led the party 2001-03

explanation.surface: A Conservative at the heart of a lot of hollow talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty speaking' gives MT because the two letters said in turn sound like 'empty'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the midst of something means being at its middle.

clue.text: Pity endless sex at a stag party?

indicators.note: endless takes the final letter off the word

parts.note: ruth is an old word for pity, still in ruthless

explanation.surface: A shame about the endless sex at a bachelor do.
explanation.walkthrough: A stag party is a British pre-wedding night out for the groom, but here the stags are deer.
explanation.definitionFit: The mating season of male deer is their period of sexual excitement.

clue.text: Rotate bum not entirely designed for stool

indicators.note: designed means newly made up, so the letters are rearranged
not entirely drops the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Swivel your backside on something designed for sitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' cuts BUM to BU, which joins ROTATE for 'designed' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A low upholstered seat without a back or arms is a type of stool.

clue.text: Every so often, find old queen for drone

indicators.note: every so often takes every other letter of the words

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the queen

explanation.surface: Now and then you find an old queen bee with her drone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Every so often' takes I, D, L from 'find old'.
explanation.definitionFit: A drone is a lazy person who does no work, like a loafer.

clue.text: Pierce organ, as would Spooner for Moses

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the starts of words, so the opening sounds trade places

parts.note: to gore is to pierce with a horn
the liver is an organ

explanation.surface: A tongue-tied cleric's mangled image of a goring for Moses.
explanation.walkthrough: GORE LIVER swaps to LORE GIVER, which in British speech sounds like LAWGIVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Moses brought the Ten Commandments down from Sinai, the giver of the law.

clue.text: C, half-cut Bush, for example, gatecrashing his party?

indicators.note: gatecrashing puts one piece inside the other, uninvited

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, the leader's party

indicators.note: half-cut chops off the second half of the word

parts.note: George Bush is an example of an American

explanation.surface: A tipsy President Bush barges into the Tory leader's party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' means drunk in British slang, but here it halves AMERICAN to AMER.
explanation.definitionFit: David Cameron led the Conservative Party from 2005 to 2016, the theme's C.

clue.text: Malicious type given bad name, that is

indicators.note: bad means corrupted, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A spiteful person has been given a bad name, as it were.
explanation.definitionFit: A mean or spiteful person is a nasty, malicious type.

clue.text: Auditor's drunk a golden drink

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the letters come from how the phrase sounds

parts.note: to neck a drink is British slang for downing it quickly

explanation.surface: An accountant has had a drink of something golden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' looks like an accountant but means a listener. In British speech 'necked a' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The drink of the gods in myth, or a sweet fruit juice, here thought of as golden.

clue.text: After a very close shave, gain for C

parts.note: after a close enough shave you are left hairless, bald
to win is to gain

explanation.surface: A narrow escape followed by a win for the Conservatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanley Baldwin led the Conservative Party between the wars, the theme's C.

clue.text: L — some dictatorial bastard from the right?

indicators.note: from the right means read from right to left, backwards
some says only part of the words is taken

explanation.surface: Some see a Labour leader as a dictatorial so-and-so of the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes RIALB from 'dictatoRIAL Bastard' and 'from the right' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Blair led the Labour Party from 1994 to 2007, the theme's L.

clue.text: Dollar leap

definitions.meaning: a horse ... when it leaps and kicks

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a dollar, and a verb for a horse's jumping kick.

clue.text: Sect suffering for C

parts.note: a church is a religious denomination or sect
ill means suffering, unwell

explanation.surface: A suffering sect hopes for a Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Winston Churchill led the Conservative Party through the Second World War, the theme's C.

clue.text: Cook red beef, not an insect

parts.note: Che Guevara was a communist revolutionary, a red

indicators.note: not takes the named letters out of the word

parts.note: a bee is an insect

explanation.surface: A recipe: cook red beef, but keep insects out.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional preparer of food in a kitchen is a cook, a synonym.

clue.text: Put down "plus room" for C?

indicators.note: the clue says the answer plus a room makes the leader, so the room is taken away from him

parts.note: a Conservative leader: Neville Chamberlain led the party 1937-40
a chamber is a room

explanation.surface: Something laid down, with extra room, for the Conservative leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads backwards: the answer 'plus room' (CHAMBER) gives C, so take CHAMBER from CHAMBERLAIN. 'Lain' is strictly from lie, not lay, so 'Put down' is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has lain somewhere has been resting there, set down.

clue.text: Much offending staff about Paul's prayer to follow

indicators.note: to follow puts the prayer after the earlier pieces
about says the staff goes round the setter's piece

parts.note: a crew is a staff of workers
Paul the setter says I'm, I is
Ave is a Latin prayer, Ave Maria

explanation.surface: The setter is concerned about crime among his staff and adds a prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul is the setter, so 'Paul's' is I'M (I is).
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden rise in crime is a lot of offending at once.

clue.text: Substance ultimately found in tree, one type of resin

indicators.note: in puts the picked letter inside the tree

parts.note: an elm is a tree

indicators.note: ultimately picks the last letter of substance

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A substance found in a tree is one kind of resin.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrant gum resin from tropical trees, used in varnishes.
